overview: In the early twentieth century, Dutch engineers and designers experimented with ways to manage water and domestic space. This chapter pairs a steam pumping station with an adaptable family home.

items.text: The Wouda pumping station opened at Lemmer in 1920 to help prevent flooding in low-lying Friesland, using steam power to move water.
The Wouda installation integrated a boiler house, chimney, fuel storage, drainage canal and sluices. Water management required an entire connected system.
Truus Schroder-Schrader commissioned the house designed by Gerrit Rietveld in Utrecht in 1924. Its design expressed ideas associated with De Stijl.
The Schroder House used a flexible internal arrangement so rooms could change with their functions. Furniture and interior space were treated as parts of one design.

sources.title: UNESCO, D.F. Wouda Steam Pumping Station
